input.quote: 13.5 Liquidated Damages. Customer acknowledges that M&I shall suffer a material adverse impact on its business if this Agreement is terminated pursuant to Sections 11.1 or 11.2(A) and that the resulting damages may not be susceptible of precise determination. Customer acknowledges that the Termination for Convenience Fee and the Termination for Cause Fee are each a reasonable approximation of such damages and shall be deemed to be liquidated damages and not a penalty.
input.rationale: Section 13.5 expressly characterises two Customer-payable fees as liquidated damages, and each is quantified as a percentage of the Estimated Remaining Value (remaining-term value) under Sections 11.1 and 11.2(A), with the Termination for Cause Fee triggered by any Event of Default. That fails the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees), and approaches walk-away territory. Deleting the fees outright would require collateral rewrites of the exit mechanics, so we cure at the fallback: 11.1 now caps the fee at three months of Fees and its applicability sentence is conformed to cross-refer to 11.2(A) (removing the Customer-default carve-out that would otherwise contradict amended 11.2(A)); 11.2(A) applies that same single fee instead of a separate remaining-value cause fee; and 13.5 confirms it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer. Notice periods, instalment timing and the existing 13.4 carve-out are left to T4C and otherwise untouched. Worth raising commercially (not a checklist element): the fee remains payable on any Customer Event of Default, however minor, so a materiality/cure qualifier would further close the minor-breach concern.

proposal.summary: Cap the early-termination fee at three months' Fees, conform 11.1's applicability sentence to amended 11.2(A), fold the separate Termination for Cause Fee into the same fee, and make it the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We replaced the remaining-term percentage penalty with our accepted three-month cap, folded the separate Termination for Cause Fee into that single fee (conforming the applicability sentence in 11.1 so it now cross-refers to 11.2(A)), and confirmed that this early-termination fee is the only liquidated amount payable by us.
